newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close up for a third day.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close up for a third day.

text.p: French stocks finished higher for the third consecutive session on Tuesday as investors took heart from some encouraging remarks by the new Socialist leaders and a drop in U.S. leading economic indicators.
Brokers said the bourse would be volatile, however, ahead of the new government's policy pronouncements and the appointment of key ministers.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 23.04 points, or 0.89 percent, at 2,624.49, helped by a rise on Wall Street triggered by the fall in April indicators that eased interest rate fears.
It has recouped around a third of its 6.5 percent fall last week.
Volume was a very heavy 9.2 billion francs.

Brokers said the market was waiting for Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's keynote address on June 17. Investors were encouraged by remarks from Elisabeth Guigou, tipped to be European Affairs minister, that the timetable for the euro would be respected.

"The fundamentals are good, and we have to stay calm," said Jean Laurent Bruel, fund manager at Banque Sifas. "Just because there's a change in government, companies aren't going to stop making profits. We have to seize opportunities."
Brokers said the market looked cheap after its 6.5 percent fall last week on indications that the left would win the parliamentary elections on Sunday.
"This is a correction. The market was oversold," said Pierre Vignaud at EIFB brokerage. He said the CAC should be valued at 2,700 points given the levels of the dollar and bond prices.
Lagardere, which slumped on Monday on concerns that the Socialists would halt privatisations, finished up 4.47 percent at 166 francs. Thomson-CSF rose 1.96 percent.
Financials steadied after falling sharply on Monday.

Consumer goods and retail stocks continued their advance on expectations a Socialist government would be positive for those sectors. Retailer Promodes added 3.87 percent to 2,067 francs, and Eridania Beghin-Say climbed 3.13 percent to 857 francs.

The partial privatisation of France Telecom, which had been scheduled by previous government to begin June 5, is effectively suspended pending the new government's decision, a France Telecom spokesman said.
